body: Almost all time is spend waiting on the following mutex: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3911e0963d39b79a85cb329340c6918397d2d05e/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_contact_listener_3d.cpp#L407 See Superluminal capture: Because you have 256 overlapping areas, there are 65K pairs it needs to process spread across 1 thread per CPU core. They all wait to be able to write to a the shared data structures `area_overlaps` , `area_enters` and `area_exits`. These data structures would need to be modified and the lock removed to make this fast.

I suppose it was just a matter of time before somebody ran into problems with that mutex. It's a bit of a naive approach on my part.

I imagine it should be possible to have `area_enters` and `area_exits` be thread-local in some way instead, and then only mutate `area_overlaps` in `_flush_area_enters`/`_flush_area_exits` instead. The same goes for the contacts I guess.

That would allow us to remove the mutex altogether.

I decided to fire up a profiler myself, and it seems there was another severe point of contention for areas at play here, namely this spin lock in `ObjectDB::get_instance` here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ee713ccb7cbaddf59f8258ed6663461779d00856/core/object/object.h#L909

... which ends up being called during `JoltArea3D::can_monitor` because of `JoltArea3D::has_area_monitor_callback` using `Callable::is_valid`, which goes through the fairly expensive trouble of checking if the target instance exists in `ObjectDB`:

```
ObjectDB::get_instance (core/object/object.h:909)
CallableCustomMethodPointer::get_object (core/object/callable_mp.h:89)
CallableCustom::is_valid (core/variant/callable.cpp:451)
Callable::is_valid (core/variant/callable.cpp:155)
JoltArea3D::has_area_monitor_callback (modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_area_3d.h:171)
JoltArea3D::is_monitoring_areas (modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_area_3d.h:175)
JoltArea3D::can_monitor (modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_area_3d.cpp:436)
JoltContactListener3D::_evaluate_area_overlap (modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_contact_listener_3d.cpp:409)
JoltContactListener3D::_try_evaluate_area_overlap (modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_contact_listener_3d.cpp:274)
JoltContactListener3D::OnContactPersisted (modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_contact_listener_3d.cpp:58)
```

Using `Callable::is_valid` in `JoltArea3D::has_*_monitor_callback` is quite overzealous though. We can almost certainly get away with a `Callable::is_null` instead, which just checks whether it's an empty reference.

I've put up a pull request for that here: #118227

I don't know if it's necessarily the most efficient way to go about it, but I (with some LLM assistance) took a stab at the thread-local approach I mentioned above, and it looks promising: #118236

When combined with #118227 I'm seeing numbers that are close enough to Godot Physics that I would call this fixed if/when both are merged. It's still ever so slightly slower, which I imagine is probably because of the shuffling of data that "has to" happen in `JoltContactListener3D`. I would need to boot into Windows to check Superluminal to say for sure though, as I can't get enough information out of Tracy's sampling on Linux. There's definitely a fair amount of `HashSet` overhead though.

I can confirm that with #118227 and #118236 the simulation is smooth on my machine. The amount of time spent in the `OnContactPersisted` callback is now only around 10% of the total time spent in `PhysicsSystem::ProcessBodyPair` (which is what dominates the sim for this demo) so to get better performance I need to start looking into the speed of the contact cache (which has been on my list for a long time).

Note that with this change, we still check `area_overlaps` 2x for every contact: once for (area1, area2) then for (area2, area1). I think we can reduce that to a single hash map lookup and I created a proof of concept [here](https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/118236_v2) (warning: badly tested). The idea is to change the HashSet into an AHashMap that stores 2 bits: if (area1, area2) collides and if (area2, area1) collides. This means we only need a single map lookup. Note that for body vs area this wastes 1 byte (+ padding), so it has pros and cons.

> Note that with this change, we still check `area_overlaps` 2x for every contact

I was just looking at doing something about that as well. :)

I think your change makes sense, at least at first glance. The bit-twiddling introduces some unfortunate complexity, but I'm not sure I can justify paying for an extra `HashSet` lookup with every removed shape pair, just to avoid that complexity.

Yes, it could use a few comments and some nice constants instead of '1' and '2' to make it a bit more clear. Also I noticed that it crashes when trying this on the MRP from 108715: I was assuming that `area_overlaps` would always contain the key by the time we try to remove a contact, but apparently not: Anyway, feel free to take or leave my change.
